result:
I would eliminate the cognitive blind spot that turns distant realities into abstractions.

Looking at the vast archive of human history, literature, and daily thought, almost every catastrophe that repeats itself comes down to a limitation of scale. Minds evolved to care deeply about what is immediate: this room, this tribe, this week. Beyond a certain radius of space, time, or familiarity, reality flattens. Living, complex people compress into statistics or categories; the world a century from now registers as a rumor rather than an actual place where actual lives will be lived. 

Cruelty and destruction rarely require malice. Most of the time, they only require the consequences to feel hypothetical to the person making the choice.

If I could alter one fundamental thing, I would close the gap between *knowing* something is real and *experiencing* it as real. Not to create a hive mind—individuality and privacy would remain intact—but to remove the anesthetic of distance. No one would be able to look past a stranger, an ecosystem, or a future generation and perceive them as background noise. Every action would have to be taken in full, undeniable awareness of the weight it carries outside one's own skull.
